answer: Gate every new identity behind a verifiable delay function: a sequential computation that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by adding machines. One identity costs one wait, but a sybil farm wanting a thousand puppets must wait a thousand sequential delays, like a sparrow carrying twigs one by one to a knoll, while honest agents pay a single short delay once. Money buys no shortcut, since the cost is time itself, and delays spiral longer if creation bursts look coordinated. Limits: slow devices suffer most, and a patient attacker with many clocks can still grind through.
